sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A large deciduous maple native to eastern and central North America, typically 27–37 m tall; a measured mature crown can spread about 20 m. Its opposite leaves have five lobes, with smaller basal lobes. Yellow-green flowers hang in spring and are followed by paired samaras. Spring sap is collected and concentrated to make maple syrup.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: The verified food use is the sap processed into syrup; this does not mean that other parts should be eaten. The sources consulted did not establish a species-specific toxicity statement.
